page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.4xlarge is a storage-focused cloud server instance provisioned via the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core. Network connectivity is supported by a 6 Gbps baseline bandwidth configuration.

A defining characteristic of the ecs.d1.4xlarge is its integrated local storage configuration, delivering 47,244 GB of direct-attached hard disk drive (HDD) capacity. The substantial magnetic storage allocation makes this instance economical for high-density bulk storage scenarios where raw volume outweighs the low-latency random access IOPS offered by solid-state drives. However, relying on HDD media introduces throughput and latency tradeoffs during random read and write operations compared to NVMe-based architectures.

The hardware profile suits big data processing, distributed file systems, data warehousing, log collection, and cold-data archiving pipelines. The combination of 16 dedicated compute cores, 64 GB memory, and tens of terabytes of local HDD capacity allows for dense storage node deployments in Hadoop, HDFS, or MapReduce topologies without requiring external network-attached block storage.

The instance features a massive local storage payload consisting of 47,244 GB of hard disk drive capacity. This architecture prioritizes cost-effective high-density capacity over the high IOPS performance of solid-state storage. Consequently, it represents a balanced option for workloads requiring large-capacity local disk space. The ecs.d1.4xlarge is suitable for big data analytics, distributed storage clusters, log processing engines, and massive data archiving workloads.
